The 300 yards handicap saw I. Badiali continue his good form to win this event very easily, and we were pleased to see Basil Walden making a welcome re-appearance on the track.

Bill Lucas put up a good performance to win the 2 miles run but he was our only competitor for this event and in the mile we had no starters! I. Badiali, our new member from India, ran well to finish second in the 440 yds. and he is certainly a most welcome addition to our ranks.
Ian Badiali was runner-up in the 440 yards, and in the one mile we saw Len Herbert and Bill Lucas outstride the opposition to come home together in first place.
Ian Badiali won the senior 440 and Bob Taylor was first home in the senior 880, while Alan Sexton, after being second in the senior 100, duly won the senior 220 yards.

We made a good start when Frank Craft won the 100 yards match event, and then Ian Badiali was first home in the 880, while Bill Lucas finished third in the one mile, after being content to amble in behind Parlett, only to get beaten up the straight for second place.
In the middle-distance events we did better, with Ian Badiali winning the quarter, Jack Brown the half-mile and Bill Lucas the mile, a very creditable trio of wins.

Wise scored a good win in the junior 880 and Ian Badiali, our new member from India, scored a popular win in the senior half-mile. His time of 1 min. 59.4 secs. was the second best time ever recorded and he is a decided asset to our ranks.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yards, with Jim Heathfield second, and Dicky Bartlett was second in the 220, while Bill Lucas was first home in the 2 miles run, with Les Stokell second.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in 2min. 0.8secs. with Don Maclean in third place, while Bill Lucas beat Len Adams in the Senior mile after a good race with Fieldsend of Mitcham A.C.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in fine style, beating Allen of Ealing H., the Middlesex champion, with Jack Brown and Ray Tooby also behind him.
Ian Badiali could only finish 4th in the 440 final which was won in 50.7 secs, and it is a pity that we are forced to run Ian at this distance as we think he prefers the half-mile.

This was held at Tooting on May 31st and was a three-sided match between Surrey A.C., Walton A.C., and ourselves. In the Senior match we had Bob Taylor winning the 440 yards in 53 seconds, while Ian Badiali won the 880 in 1 min. 59 secs.
The 880 yards saw three of our members running, and they all did well although only one of them, Bob Taylor, qualified for the final of this race. Ian Badiali and P.
Basil Walden won both the Senior sprint events with Ian Badiali first home in the 880 in 2 min. 1.9 secs., and Alan Sexton winning the 440 in 52.1 secs.; shades of things to come!
Walden, I.

Ian Badiali was second in the 440 but we were short of competitors for the two field events which were included in the match. On the same day we had a team in the 2 miles team race at the S.T.C., and with Bill Lucas 1st, Len Herbert 4th and John Bromley 6th, we were first wth 11 pts., against Essex…

Ian Badiali and Bob Taylor gave us the lead over the first two legs, but Wint got by Alan Sexton, but not by much, so that our last man, Bagnall, went off on Laing's heels only to find that the Jamaican was not trying and before he realised this the rest of the field had closed up and he had to figh…
Basil Walden won the 100 yds., beating Gibbs, of Herne Hill, and the latter was also beaten by Alan Sexton in the 220. Jack Brown and Ian Badiali were 2nd and 3rd in the 880, and A.

Ian Badiali was second with Alan Bishop third, but a very small field turned out for this event, and we wonder if members appreciate the fact that we give standard medals in all our championship races in order to encourage our members to take part.
Bob Taylor was 2nd with Ian Badiali 4th in the 880, and Don Maclean was 2nd in the 1 mile. Our team also won the 2 miles team race with Jack Brown first man home in the good time of 9 min. 16.4 secs.

Ian Badiali won the 880 in 1 min. 58.6 secs., and as he was our only runner, it was just as well that he came in first. The 1 mile also saw only one Belgrave representative in Ray Tooby, but here again he was more than a match for the opposition, and Ray won in the good time of 4 min. 21 secs.
Morrell in the senior 100 yds., with Ian Badiali and Don Maclean as our 220 men, but they failed to score a win and Mac’s finishing leap was something to see!
Ian Badiali won the 440 yds. in the good time of 51.5 secs., and Jack Brown was second to Terry Higgins in the 880 in 1 min. 57 secs., with Alan Bishop in third place
Ian Badiali won his 440 yds. heat in 51.9 secs., and was placed 5th in the final, which was in 49 seconds by Arthur Wint who was running for the Hospitals.

Ian Badiali won the Shipping A.A. 440 yards championship in 52.1 seconds, and Len Rolls won the Veterans A.C. 880 yards championship. Ted Smith won the London Transport 7 miles Walk Championship at Wembley in record time.
Ian Badiali was first home in the 1st string 660 yards in 87.4 secs., and Bob Taylor recorded 86.5, to set up a new track record in the second race over this distance.

Wolton beat both Bob Taylor and Ian Badiali and is showing great improvement this season. In the Senior 880 yards we saw John Bromley score rather a surprise win in the good time of 2 mins. 0.8 sec., with Ian Badiali second and Chas.

Ivan Mayers won the 100 yds., with Dicky Bartlett winning the 220, and Ian Badiali was 1st in the 880, with Ray Tooby in 3rd place. Bob Taylor was 2nd in the 1 mile, with John Burr 3rd, and George Stace ran well to win the 2 miles run in 9 mins. 58 secs.

Basil Walden qualified for the 100 final, but could only finish 6th in a close race, and Denis Merrett was 2nd in the 220 final, being beaten by Clay Gibbs, of Herne Hill H. Bob Taylor ran a fine race to win the 880 yds. in 1 min. 59.6 secs, with Ian Badiali in 4th place.
Dicky also won the 440 yds., beating Ian Badiali, and Jim Heathfield was 3rd in the 880, with Don Maclean 2nd in the 1 mile in 4 mins. 26.9 secs.

Gaworski also did well with 2nd place in the Weight, 3rd in the Discus, and 2nd place in the Hammer Throw, which made for a busy afternoon's work. Denis Merrett was 2nd in the 220 yds. final, and Ian Badiali was 3rd in the 880 yds.

The following evening, at Motspur Park, we fielded a team in a 1 mile medley relay and Ian Badiali gave us the lead over the half-mile stage, then Ian Forrester and Dicky Bartlett did the two 220's with "Jock" Cameron running the quarter, and we eventually finished 3rd.
Tranter ran in the 440 yds. match and was 3rd in a close run race. Ian Badiali won an Invitation 600 yds. scratch race, and he beat A.
Bob Taylor was our "highlight" of the meeting, when he did 1 min. 55.8 secs. to finish 2nd in the 880 yds., and Ian Badiali was unlucky not to qualify in his heat.
Ian Badiali did 1 min. 58.6 secs. in his heat, but did not qualify, and it may well be that a better method would be to take times rather than placings.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 59.1 secs., but nearly lost the race by easing at the tape, and Chas. Walker ran well to win the 1 mile in the good time of 4 mins. 22 secs.

Ian Badiali and Pete Cornish were also the only two present for the 1 mile medley relay, and so we also had to scratch from this. Bob Taylor ran a fine race to win the 880 yds. in 1 min. 55.8 secs., with Ian Badiali in 3rd place, and Bob was given a Striking Clock, with Ian taking an Easipower Toaster.
In the 880 yds. we had Ian Badiali and Bob Taylor, but with the slowest of the four heats being 1 min. 55.4 secs., neither of our runners could qualify for the final.
We sadly missed Alan Sexton, still out in Canada, while Ian Badiali was away on holiday and " Jock " was just getting over his leg trouble, so we hope for better luck next year.
Cameron score a good win from Bob Wolton in 51.6 secs., with Ian Badiali in third place.
Our team of Ian Badiali, Ron Morrell, Bob Wolton and " Jock " Cameron also won the 1 mile scratch relay in the good time of 3 mins. 36.8 secs.

John Bromley took the 880 yards in 1:59.6 from I.Badiali and Chas. Walker and then the 1 mile in 4:24.8 from 'Jumbo' Masters and Cliff Roffey.
